=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh: the new `_autofix_pr_named_review_runs` function (~lines 1208–1248 in the post-diff file), specifically the jq filter: | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `_autofix_pr_named_review_runs` can count a PR-named `workflow_dispatch` run from an arbitrary branch and a workflow path with a matching basename as a legitimate review run.
  WHY: This differs from the poller helper’s exact-path and default-branch provenance checks, allowing a spoofed run to suppress a legitimate retrigger or consume the changes-lost retry budget.
- scripts/smoke_review_dispatch.sh: the new `smoke_review_checked_out_sha` function (the file is "MODIFIED: lines 1-220 (1 hunks, ~220 lines changed)" per the symbol diff, but the full content is not inlined in the diff snippets — the function is referenced from `test-and-mark-stable.yml` Phase 4 leg (c) and Phase 4b correlation) | severity=critical | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: It is unclear whether `smoke_review_checked_out_sha` passes `--allow-escape-sequences` (or equivalent) on every `gh api .../actions/jobs/<id>/logs` call.
  WHY: The source says the fix may already be present, but if it is missing, real job logs with ANSI escape sequences cause correlation to fail and Phase 4b to end as `retry_run_unverified`.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml: lines ~6232–6268 ("Re-trigger review via workflow_dispatch" step) and lines ~6383–6405 ("Re-dispatch review on editor-changes-lost" step), both of which now end with: | severity=high | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: It is unclear whether the extracted changes-lost redispatch script preserves the `CHANGES_LOST_REDISPATCHED` write to `$GITHUB_ENV`.
  WHY: The source does not include the new script bodies, and if the write is missing, the subsequent Telegram warning step may take a different message path.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: `_pr_named_review_default_branch` (lines ~17400–17415 in the post-diff file): | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: When `.default_branch` is JSON `null`, the helper treats the literal string `null` as a resolved branch and does not log the promised `default_branch_unresolved` provenance diagnostic.
  WHY: The downstream lookup fails open, but operators debugging absent PR-named matches will not see the diagnostic line.
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml: Phase 4b retry correlation block (lines ~2694–2754 in the post-diff file): | severity=high | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: If `DEADLINE` is not assigned earlier in the Phase 4b `run:` block, the numeric comparison can treat a transient log-read failure as an expired deadline.
  WHY: The source cannot verify whether the assignment exists in the unseen preamble; if it does not, the retry loop fails on its first transient read instead of retrying.
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh: `_autofix_pr_named_review_runs` (the function body around line 1238): | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The helper fetches the latest 100 `workflow_dispatch` runs across all branches and workflows without a server-side branch filter.
  WHY: Under heavy dispatch traffic, unrelated runs can fill the page and hide a legitimate review dispatch, causing peer detection or retry-budget accounting to miss it.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: `_pr_named_review_dispatch_runs` (lines ~17423–17516 in the post-diff file) — the return-shape change at: | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The helper’s output shape changed from the prior `gh run list` shape to a REST-shaped object.
  WHY: Callers still using `.id` or `.display_title` would receive empty fields, and the plan’s claim that the shape is unchanged misleads future contributors.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

- scripts/gh_helpers.sh: the new `_autofix_pr_named_review_runs` function (~lines 1208–1248 in the post-diff file), specifically the jq filter:

  Why it fails at runtime: A spoofed run can be counted as a peer, skipping a legitimate retrigger, or as a completed run, consuming the changes-lost retry budget.
  severity=high | confidence=4
- scripts/smoke_review_dispatch.sh: the new `smoke_review_checked_out_sha` function (the file is "MODIFIED: lines 1-220 (1 hunks, ~220 lines changed)" per the symbol diff, but the full content is not inlined in the diff snippets — the function is referenced from `test-and-mark-stable.yml` Phase 4 leg (c) and Phase 4b correlation)
  Problem: It is unclear whether every `gh api .../actions/jobs/<id>/logs` call uses `--allow-escape-sequences` (or equivalent).
  Why it fails at runtime: If the fix is absent, real logs with ANSI escape sequences make correlation fail, causing Phase 4b to end as `retry_run_unverified`; if present, this is a no-op check.
  severity=critical | confidence=3

  Why it fails at runtime: If the write is missing, the subsequent Telegram warning step may take a different message path.
  severity=high | confidence=2
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: `_pr_named_review_default_branch` (lines ~17400–17415 in the post-diff file):
  Problem: If `.default_branch` is `null`, the helper treats the literal string `null` as non-empty and does not log the promised unresolved-branch diagnostic.
  Why it fails at runtime: Matching fails open, but operators debugging absent PR-named matches will not find the diagnostic line.
  severity=low | confidence=3
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml: Phase 4b retry correlation block (lines ~2694–2754 in the post-diff file):
  Problem: It is unclear whether `DEADLINE` is assigned earlier in the separate Phase 4b `run:` block.
  Why it fails at runtime: If unset, a transient read may be treated as an expired deadline on the first attempt, preventing retries.
  severity=high | confidence=2
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh: `_autofix_pr_named_review_runs` (the function body around line 1238):
  Problem: The helper queries the latest 100 `workflow_dispatch` runs across the repository without a branch or workflow filter.

  severity=high | confidence=3
